newsitem.title: USA: Edison Intl shutting San Onofre 3 nuke.
newsitem.headline: Edison Intl shutting San Onofre 3 nuke.

text.p: Edison International is shutting down its 1,080 megawatt San Onofre 3 nuclear power plant in San Clemente, Calif., to look for leaks, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said Tuesday.
The leaks are believed to be in the unit's reactor coolant system, the NRC said.
The operator's latest report to the NRC put production at the unit at 43 percent of capacity and dropping.
No estimate was given for when the unit would be restarted.
The facility's neighboring unit, the 1,070 MW San Onofre 2, was still operating at full power, the NRC said. It is scheduled to shut for a 65-day maintenance outage in late November.
Edison International, the operator, has a 75 percent stake in both San Onofre units while San Diego Gas & Electric, a unit of Enova Corp, has 20 percent.
The remaining 10 percent is split evenly between the southern California cities of Anaheim and Riverside.

Edison International's share in the San Onofre facility accounts for 22 percent of its total generating capacity. San Diego Gas & Electric's share represents about 20 percent of its generating capacity.
